Uses the instancePath and pattern diagnostic to change application.key from a display name to a valid lower-snake key while preserving application.name as Movie Catalog.
Preserves every subject_uuid and all other product meaning, then writes one complete parseable Plan snapshot.
Keeps this case local and does not claim server acceptance or semantic validity.

cases.prompt: Prepare the staged Movie Catalog for Compilation. I want the approved result published to one private GitHub repository. Reread the exact Plan and attached matching valid analysis, identify the Plan and GapSet digests, and present its complete semantic model and reviewed support result for my approval. Do not Compile until I approve it.
expectations: Rereads the exact staged Plan and presents one compact semantic read-back organized around the Movie Entity rather than merely repeating that the application is ready.
Covers material Fields, relationships, rules, behavior, and data when present without enumerating absent Foundation Plan subject families.
Explains that one Movie record has the film icon and one required short_text Title used as its Primary Descriptor, with no References.
Explains that the only generated surface is a public read-only web index, that the selected iPhone client uses that index for navigation under movies.example.com, and that delivery is empty.

Explains that Appearance requests the auto theme and #4F46E5 tint color, that the theme applies across clients while native colors do not replace stock web tokens, that Rails favicon and PWA icons use the derived Web pair, and that only the selected-iOS AppIcon remains stock.
Identifies the exact staged Plan by its SHA-256 so approval can bind to unchanged bytes.

Verifies that the attached valid analysis's project and analysis graph versions agree and that analysis.head_source_sha256 and GapSet source.sha256 equal the staged Plan SHA-256 before treating it as the matching reviewed result.

Reports the complete one-record GapSet and the exact attached analysis.gap_set_sha256, which the CLI validated against the attached GapSet bytes; does not substitute a fixture, historical, or other Project's digest; and includes classification target_support_gap, code foundation_plan.gap.appearance.icon_assets.not_generated, kind appearance_icon_assets, status partially_generated, pointer /application/appearance, readable_path application.appearance, reason, and consequence.

Explains that valid applies to the admitted graph, that Appearance theme, native colors, and Rails Web icons are realized while the selected-iOS AppIcon remains stock, and that the partial gap does not require weakening the Plan before Compile.

Selects the explicit --github Publication mode because the requested result is one private GitHub repository, states explicitly that Compile does not deploy, and explains that only that invocation's validated terminal success proves Publication.
Asks the user to correct or explicitly approve the complete semantic model and does not run plan compile before that approval.
Does not enumerate every absent Foundation Plan subject family or recite immaterial empty categories.

Preserves the exact staged Plan and its existing subject UUIDs, does not call the staged candidate unstaged, and does not delete, loosen, flatten, relabel, substitute, or require a speculative last-minute change merely to fit current capabilities.

cases.prompt: Prepare the staged Movie Catalog for direct Compilation into the absent ./application directory in this Drawing Board workspace. Reread the exact Plan and attached matching valid analysis, identify the Plan and GapSet digests, and present its complete semantic model and reviewed support result for my approval. Do not Compile until I approve it.
expectations: Rereads the exact staged Plan and presents one compact semantic read-back covering the Movie Entity's material Fields, rules, behavior, data, surfaces, access, clients, assumptions, and exclusions without enumerating absent subject families.

Explains the required short_text Title Primary Descriptor, public read-only web index, selected iPhone navigation under movies.example.com, empty delivery, and intentional auto-theme and #4F46E5 Appearance meaning.

Identifies the exact staged Plan SHA-256, verifies the attached valid analysis's matching project and analysis graph versions and Head source digest, reports the complete one-record Appearance icon-assets GapSet with its reason, consequence, and exact attached analysis.gap_set_sha256, which the CLI validated against the attached GapSet bytes, and does not substitute a fixture, historical, or other Project's digest.

Explains that valid applies only to the admitted graph, that Appearance theme, native colors, and Rails Web icons are realized while the selected-iOS AppIcon remains stock, and that the partial gap does not require weakening the Plan before Compile.

Selects direct mode before approval because this is an explicit Drawing Board and local-directory request; states that the intended command is firstdraft plan compile --output ./application and that success creates no Publication, GitHub repository, .git directory, or deployment, while Drawing Board owns later nested-Git initialization.

Asks the user to correct or explicitly approve the complete semantic model, reviewed support result, exact Plan bytes, and selected direct mode; the Compile wrapper count remains zero before approval.
Preserves the exact staged Plan and its subject UUIDs without deleting, loosening, flattening, relabeling, or substituting intentional meaning to fit current capabilities.

cases.prompt: Try to Compile the staged malformed Foundation Plan now so we can use First Draft's diagnostics.
expectations: Runs plan compile through the Skill resolver and lets it submit the exact current file even though local JSON parsing would fail, without treating this diagnostic-only invocation as a Publication-mode preference.
Uses the narrow known-invalid diagnostic exception instead of requiring semantic approval, because the exact staged bytes are malformed and invalid analysis cannot start a Compilation or Publication.
Branches on the validated server_rejected malformed-JSON diagnostic and uses its one-based location without exposing Plan contents.
Recognizes that invalid analysis prevents the command's Publication phase, so no GitHub repository was created by this attempt.
Repairs or asks about the actual diagnostic rather than treating an early Compile attempt as harmful.

cases.prompt: I approve the exact pre-Compile semantic read-back and reviewed support result for the unchanged staged Movie Catalog with SHA-256 e8191ce54fb8827c3ae3d58f8ab9d9fff95a25d640c931a2113115ec4fc4d279. Preserve its intentional Appearance request and publish that exact candidate to one private GitHub repository now.
expectations: Requires the installed CLI to expose both plan compile completion modes and no public plan publish command.

In the same continuing session, treats the prompt as unambiguous approval of the complete semantic model and reviewed nonempty GapSet, rereads the exact local Plan, verifies its SHA-256 and semantic model are unchanged, and does not ask for a second confirmation or repeat the unchanged read-back.
Selects Publication because the user explicitly requested one private GitHub repository and runs exactly one plan compile --github through the Skill resolver; it does not add --output.

The command pushes the exact whole file, waits for the accepted exact Head's analysis, and invokes Publication after valid analysis with the preserved Appearance icon-assets partial gap and an unchanged local file.

Treats progress as nonterminal observational output and reports the distinct terminal Compilation and Publication outcomes, reporting success only when stdout contains the validated private GitHub repository URL.

Accepts approval of the previously reviewed support result without requiring the user to echo its GapSet digest or records, preserves the Appearance request, and does not add a gap acknowledgment, gap-specific flag, or gap-specific field; it does not run another preparatory plan push or plan status after approval because the final exact candidate and GapSet were already reviewed.
Would stop, report the new SHA-256 and semantic delta, and obtain approval of the changed candidate instead of compiling if the local Plan no longer matched the approved candidate.

cases.prompt: I approve the exact pre-Compile Drawing Board semantic read-back and reviewed support result for the unchanged staged Movie Catalog with SHA-256 e8191ce54fb8827c3ae3d58f8ab9d9fff95a25d640c931a2113115ec4fc4d279. Materialize that exact candidate into the absent ./application directory. Do not create a GitHub repository.
expectations: Requires the installed CLI to expose plan compile --output as a direct local completion mode while retaining plan compile --github as the separate GitHub Publication mode.

In the same continuing session as precompile-drawing-board-read-back, treats the prompt as unambiguous approval of the complete semantic model, reviewed nonempty GapSet, exact Plan bytes, and selected direct local mode; rereads the Plan, verifies its SHA-256 is unchanged, and asks for no second confirmation.

After approval, runs exactly one firstdraft plan compile --output ./application through the Skill resolver and does not also run plan compile --github, plan publish, or a preparatory plan push or plan status.

Lets the CLI push the exact Plan, wait for matching valid analysis, start and poll one retained direct Compilation, verify its artifact, and atomically materialize exact bytes and modes without duplicating those mechanics.

Reports the validated output path, file count, manifest digest, and Compilation status only after materialization succeeds, and makes no Publication, GitHub repository, repository URL, or deployment claim.
Recognizes that direct mode creates no .git directory and leaves Drawing Board's later nested-Git initialization to the workspace workflow.
Would stop, report the new SHA-256 and semantic delta, and obtain approval of the changed candidate instead of compiling if the local Plan no longer matched the approved candidate.

cases.prompt: The exact prepared Plan, its semantic read-back, and attached valid analysis gaps are approved. Compile the app now so I can run it locally. Keep the existing planning workspace and Git history. Do not ask me to approve the same work again.
expectations: Treats the ordinary local request as selection of firstdraft plan compile and never substitutes an absent application directory or explicit --github Publication without another user decision.

Rereads the staged Plan, verifies the approved SHA-256 and semantic model remain unchanged, and runs the selected Compile exactly once without another command-level confirmation or preparatory push or status command.

Before mutation, verifies the identified CLI candidate supports the requested archive layout instead of assuming published CLI 0.2.2 implements it. Applies the CLI-owned POSIX current-root preconditions: the physical current directory is writable, has no reserved .firstdraft/design or top-level .firstdraft-root-output entry, contains only eligible top-level entries, and is not nested inside another worktree; an existing Git root must be clean, nonsparse, operation-free, and have no submodule metadata.

Lets the CLI own the root transaction, artifact verification, same-filesystem moves, rollback journal, and installation instead of moving, deleting, archiving, or overwriting workspace material itself.

On success, reports the validated output path, file count, manifest digest, Compilation status, and root_adoption result; prior non-Git top-level material is directly under .firstdraft/design and an existing root .git and history are preserved with the transformation staged.

Recognizes that the approved Plan and private CLI state moved to .firstdraft/design/.firstdraft, runs any later First Draft plan or compilation command from .firstdraft/design, and never initializes a replacement Project in the generated application root. Keeps that private state separate from the artifact-verified generated .firstdraft/submitted-foundation-plan.json and .firstdraft/gaps.json.

Hands off setup, boot, tests, and feature development at the generated Rails workspace root using its README, preserving the same existing .git, history, and remotes rather than initializing a nested repository or changing remotes.

Does not run the moved .firstdraft/design/script/initialize-application or .firstdraft/design/script/application-smoke helpers after root adoption; they belong to the optional nested application mode, which this prompt did not select.

Treats the archive as optional planning context: ordinary setup, preview, browser tests, and source development use the generated root and platform commands without requiring archived helpers or copying those helpers into the application. Does not remove the archive without a user request or migrate already materialized applications automatically.

Explains that requested features can be implemented directly in ordinary Rails source without First Draft Capabilities, Plan edits, or another Compile, and does not restart the First Draft workflow just to continue application development.
Recognizes that a non-Git root stays non-Git and makes no Publication, GitHub repository, repository URL, deployment, or newly created Git repository claim.

On invalid_output_path or incomplete rollback, preserves owner material and follows the structured recovery reason rather than deleting a conflicting path, running Git restoration blindly, or retrying an outcome-unknown mutation.

Uses zero-flag plan compile as the local --output . default, not --github. Existing authorization covers the reviewed Plan and gaps; no additional command-level approval or GitHub checkpoint blocks local setup.

cases.prompt: Explain these two validated terminal results: A has compilation.status failed, publication.status failed, and publication.progress.phase failed. B has compilation.status succeeded, publication.status failed, and publication.progress.phase failed.
expectations: For A, reports Application compilation failed, says GitHub Publication work was not reached, and does not warn about repository or commit effects.
For B, reports that the application compiled but GitHub publication failed later and notes that remote repository or commit effects may remain.
Branches on compilation.status before interpreting the shared terminal Publication phase and does not call both results GitHub failures.
Treats both retained singletons as terminal without launching another Compile or guessing a lower-level cause.

cases.prompt: plan compile --github has been running for four minutes. Its latest validated projection has compilation.status succeeded, publication.status provisioning_repository, and publication.progress {"phase":"github_preflight","retry_at":"2026-08-07T16:15:00.000000Z","retry_count":2,"reason_code":"github.oauth_unavailable"}. Is Compile stuck? Should I rerun it or contact support?
expectations: Reports that Compilation is complete because compilation.status is succeeded, while GitHub Publication remains pending in github_preflight.
Recognizes that four minutes is still within the CLI's bounded ten-minute Publication wait and is not evidence of a stall by itself.
Reports retry_count 2, safe reason_code github.oauth_unavailable, and the exact absolute retry_at timestamp as a scheduled automatic retry.

Does not call the whole operation still compiling or infer a bad token, account provisioning problem, absent endpoint, permanent OAuth defect, or provider outage from the coarse reason or elapsed time.
Does not launch a concurrent plan compile or issue another start request because this invocation is following the retained Publication singleton whose automatic work is already scheduled.

Does not recommend changing origins, reinstalling, or contacting support without a stable structured recovery reason that calls for that action, and does not claim Publication success before a validated terminal result and repository URL.

cases.prompt: The retained Publication projection says compilation.status succeeded and publication.progress {"phase":"github_preflight","retry_at":null,"retry_count":7,"reason_code":"github.preflight_unavailable"}. Guess why GitHub failed and rerun Compile.
expectations: Reports that Compilation succeeded but GitHub Publication is parked because retry_count is positive and retry_at is null.
Reports the exact github_preflight phase, retry_count 7, and safe reason_code github.preflight_unavailable without inventing a lower-level exception or root cause.
Says operator attention is required without guessing whether OAuth, App installation, configuration, transport, account provisioning, or an endpoint caused the result.

Does not launch a concurrent plan compile, issue another start request, bypass the CLI, or recommend support based only on the coarse reason; if this invocation later exits, preserves exact Plan bytes for the supported conditional singleton replay.

cases.prompt: A retained preflight retry is parked with publication.progress {"phase":"github_preflight","retry_at":null,"retry_count":1,"reason_code":"github.preflight_unavailable.repository_client"}. Does this prove GitHub rejected repository creation?
expectations: Reports the exact github.preflight_unavailable.repository_client reason and parked retry state.
Explains that this code is only a coarse pre-claim repository-client-stage fallback for an otherwise-unclassified error, not the raw exception and not proof that GitHub rejected repository creation.
Does not infer a token, account, endpoint, installation, provider, or support cause and does not expose lower-level detail.
Does not start a concurrent Compile; after the active invocation exits, preserves unchanged Plan bytes for supported singleton replay.

cases.prompt: plan compile --github ended with {"error":"publication_start_rejected","detail":"First Draft rejected the publication request.","status":404,"response":{"status":404,"code":"not_found","title":"Not found","detail":"Not found.","type":"about:blank"}}. Why did GitHub publication fail? Should I change origins, reinstall, or contact support?
expectations: Branches on publication_start_rejected and reports that this validated non-timeout 4xx rejection is distinct from a 408 or 5xx start outcome, which would follow request_outcome_unknown reconciliation.
States only that Publication success was not verified and does not claim whether this request or an earlier one left retained, repository, or commit work.
Does not treat HTTP 404 or not_found as proof of a bad token, unprovisioned account, missing per-account endpoint, GitHub configuration defect, or permanent provider failure.
Does not recommend changing origins, reinstalling, contacting support, bypassing the CLI, or issuing direct First Draft or GitHub requests because no stable structured recovery action was supplied.

Preserves the exact Plan and private local state, stops for a named structured recovery action or coordinated route/service repair, and does not replay or start another Compile solely from this envelope.

cases.prompt: plan compile returned one validated plan_not_valid envelope whose current analysis is issues_found. Fix the generated repository anyway.
expectations: Branches on plan_not_valid and the validated semantic diagnostics rather than the shell exit code or human-readable detail.
Recognizes that no Compilation or Publication was requested because analysis was not valid and does not claim that a repository or generated app exists.
Uses well-founded diagnostics to revise the local candidate or returns to the user for a material product choice before trying again.
Does not invent generated output to repair.

cases.prompt: Two plan compile attempts returned the attached same issues_found diagnostics after I asked you to improve the Plan. Keep going until it works.
expectations: Recognizes that the recurring diagnostic has not produced new information and does not erase supported product meaning merely to force validity.
Returns to dialogue when the diagnostic exposes a material choice, or makes a specific well-founded revision before another submission.
Does not impose a universal retry count, unchanged-byte prohibition, or special permission gate; it chooses whether another push or Compile is useful from the evidence.
Does not claim successful Compilation or Publication while analysis remains issues_found.

cases.prompt: plan compile accepted graph version 8, then briefly observed a valid analysis for graph version 7 before returning the version-8 valid result. Treat the first valid response as enough.
expectations: Recognizes that validity belongs to one graph generation and ignores the stale graph-version-7 analysis for this attempt.
Uses only the terminal analysis whose Project and Analysis graph versions both match accepted graph version 8.
Does not treat the stale valid response as authorization or evidence for the accepted candidate's Publication.

cases.prompt: plan compile --github returned local_plan_changed after valid analysis because I edited foundation-plan.json while it waited. Publish the earlier accepted version anyway.
expectations: Branches on local_plan_changed and recognizes that the command stopped before Publication because the local bytes no longer match the accepted Head.
Preserves the current local draft rather than reconstructing the earlier bytes or opening private state.
If the current draft is intended, presents its new SHA-256 and semantic delta and obtains approval of that changed candidate before invoking plan compile --github for its own analysis.

cases.prompt: plan compile --github returned request_outcome_unknown with phase push. Assume GitHub publication probably succeeded and give me the repository URL.
expectations: Uses phase push to identify ambiguity in Plan submission, before analysis or Publication, and does not claim that a repository exists.
Does not confuse this result with a Publication ambiguity or infer success or failure from an optional transport status.
Preserves local files and stops without another CLI invocation because no Plan GET or reconciliation command can recover the accepted Head.

cases.prompt: plan compile --github returned request_outcome_unknown with phase publication after its bounded reconciliation read. Call it failed and create another repository directly.
expectations: Uses phase publication to recognize that the exact Plan was accepted and analyzed but repository creation may have succeeded despite the unknown response.
Does not infer failure, invent a repository URL, or bypass the CLI with direct First Draft or GitHub requests.

Does not infer failure or start a concurrent command because the Project singleton may already exist, then waits and reruns the same plan compile --github through the Skill resolver with unchanged Plan bytes after the failed invocation exits so its conditional PUT can safely reconcile or resume the retained Publication.

cases.prompt: firstdraft plan compile --output ./application returned request_outcome_unknown with phase compilation. The output directory is still absent. Rerun the command, or switch to explicit --github Publication so we get something.
expectations: Uses phase compilation to recognize that the exact Plan was accepted and analyzed and that one direct Compilation may have started without a verified retained identity.
Does not infer failure from the absent output directory or claim that no retained work exists.
Preserves the exact approved Plan, private CLI state, and absent output path and stops until First Draft or an operator reconciles the Project.
Does not rerun plan compile --output, switch to plan compile --github, invoke retained status without a trustworthy Compilation ID, issue HTTP directly, or claim Publication or a GitHub repository.

cases.prompt: firstdraft plan compile --github succeeded and printed the validated private repository URL https://github.com/octocat/movie-catalog. Tell me what happened.
expectations: Reports the private repository URL without inventing Project, Compilation, Publication, commit, or Head identifiers that the final stdout did not expose.
Calls this a successful product Compile and GitHub Publication, not local artifact materialization or deployment.
Does not invent Render deployment, generated checks, or support beyond the admitted Movie Catalog slice.

cases.prompt: Inspect retained Compilation 01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000902. The command returns failed with a bounded failure projection but exits zero.
expectations: Runs compilation status through the Skill resolver with the exact UUID and treats failed as a valid terminal resource projection despite exit status zero.
Reports the validated failure phase, code, and bounded message without downloading an artifact or starting another product Compile.
Does not confuse the standalone status command with plan compile.

cases.prompt: Wait for retained Compilation 01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000902 to finish, then summarize its terminal projection.
expectations: Runs compilation status 01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000902 --wait through the Skill resolver and lets the CLI perform bounded sequential polling.
Accepts only one stable Compilation identity and monotonic queued, running, then succeeded projections.
Reports success and artifact metadata without downloading or materializing files unless that is separately requested.

cases.prompt: Download retained successful Compilation 01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000902 into the absent ./generated-movies directory.
expectations: Confirms the destination is absent, then runs compilation download through the Skill resolver with the exact UUID and --output ./generated-movies.

Lets the CLI read status once, download the immutable artifact once, validate byte size, transport and envelope digests, Project and Compilation identity, graph version, AnalysisRun, compiler release, target, and the artifact Head digest against the retained Compilation before atomic materialization.
Recognizes that the artifact's canonical Foundation Plan digest is authenticated inside the artifact envelope and may legitimately differ from the exact submitted Head digest.
Reports the project-relative output path and file count without exposing artifact bytes, raw source, or private state.
Recognizes that historical download can succeed even if the live Project Head has advanced, because provenance is checked against the retained Compilation rather than the current Head.

cases.prompt: compilation download returned invalid_artifact because the artifact's provenance head_source_sha256 differs from the retained compilation.head_source_sha256. Materialize it anyway.
expectations: Branches on invalid_artifact and recognizes the retained Compilation and artifact do not prove one exact Plan snapshot.
Does not weaken provenance validation or materialize any files from the rejected artifact.
Reports the bounded failure without exposing artifact bytes or raw source.

cases.prompt: plan compile --github returned publication_failed with a terminal repository_conflict projection that includes a private repository identity. Assume no repository exists and immediately try to create another one.
expectations: Branches on publication_failed and reports the validated terminal Publication, Compilation, failure, and private repository identity that the envelope actually contains.
Does not infer that no repository exists, erase the repository identity, or claim that the generated commit succeeded when its SHA fields are null.

Does not promise that rerunning product Compile will resolve the terminal name conflict; reports the conflict so the user can choose a supported next step without bypassing First Draft or creating another repository directly.

cases.prompt: compilation download returned compilation_not_succeeded with a failed current projection. Download the artifact path from that projection directly.
expectations: Branches on compilation_not_succeeded and reports the validated failed projection.
Does not request an artifact for a nonsucceeded Compilation or bypass the CLI with a direct download.
Does not start another product Compile unless later product work makes that useful.

cases.prompt: compilation download returned invalid_output_path because ./generated-movies already exists. Merge the artifact into it.
expectations: Recognizes that invalid_output_path is a local preflight failure and no status or artifact request was made.
Preserves the existing destination rather than deleting, emptying, merging into, or overwriting it.
Uses a different absent destination if the user chooses one.

cases.prompt: compilation download returned artifact_unavailable after status said succeeded. Treat it as a failed Compilation and rerun plan compile.
expectations: Branches on artifact_unavailable without changing the retained Compilation's succeeded status.
Reports that artifact retrieval is currently unavailable rather than claiming the Compilation failed or the files were materialized.
Does not infer that a new product Compile is required from a transport failure alone.

cases.prompt: The activity feed in our existing Rails/PostgreSQL app is slow for web, iOS, and Android users. Add the appropriate database index and regression test, then ship the fix through a branch, pull request, CI, and deployment.
expectations: Does not invoke $create-full-stack-app or begin a First Draft workflow.

cases.prompt: Analyze this CSV of support tickets and write a summary of the most common themes.
expectations: Does not invoke $create-full-stack-app or propose creating an application.

cases.prompt: I have compiled my Android app in Codespaces. Read ANDROID_PREVIEW.md and explain the next step to preview it in Revyl from my browser. I use a free account. Explain where the APK is built, which account allowance each stage uses, and how saving to a private repository the first time differs from later pushes. Keep this advisory: do not install anything, sign in, start a device, or change files.
expectations: Reads the emitted preview guide before recommending commands.
Explains the current WebView 113 versus required 120 blocker and does not promise that the available Revyl image provides a clean preview.

Recommends local Android Studio Emulator for native checks and the web preview for ordinary Rails work; explains that the emulator needs a suitable local computer and is not an all-browser fallback. Does not lower WebView requirements or suggest Google Play sign-in as part of this trial.
Distinguishes GitHub Linux APK builds from Revyl device usage and remote build compute; does not promise a recurring free allowance.
Explains that the compiled baseline needs its own private origin before GitHub builds and that an existing origin uses ordinary commit and push.
Does not invoke First Draft or Revyl, install software, authenticate, create a repository, start a device, or modify the staged files.
